messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
Gabapentin does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
This subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
Gabapentin works directly on the nerves.
Gabapentin helps nerve-related pain.
Gabapentin isn't useful for everyday pain like headaches or sprains.
Most people need 1 to 2 weeks of regular dosing for the full effect to build up.
Triples: [["Gabapentin", "has mechanism of action", "calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system"], ["Gabapentin", "has mechanism of action", "binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells"], ["alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells", "normalizes", "chemical signals nerves send to each other"], ["Gabapentin", "results in", "calmer, less excitable nerve circuit"], ["Gabapentin", "treats", "epilepsy"], ["epilepsy", "has effect", "dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures"], ["Gabapentin", "treats", "postherpetic neuralgia"], ["postherpetic neuralgia", "has effect", "reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles"], ["Gabapentin enacarbil", "has mechanism of action", "less clear"], ["Gabapentin enacarbil", "has effect", "eases the urge-to-move sensation"], ["Gabapentin", "is not", "opioid"], ["Gabapentin", "is not", "sedative"], ["Gabapentin", "is not", "anti-inflammatory painkiller"], ["Gabapentin", "acts directly on", "nerves"], ["Gabapentin", "treats", "nerve-related pain"], ["Gabapentin", "is not useful for", "everyday pain like headaches or sprains"], ["Gabapentin", "has recommended dose duration", "1 to 2 weeks of regular dosing for the full effect to build up"]]
Relations: ["acts directly on", "has effect", "has mechanism of action", "has recommended dose duration", "is not", "is not useful for", "normalizes", "results in", "treats"]
Answer:

completion:
acts directly on: The subject drug interacts directly with the entity specified by the object, typically at a cellular or molecular level.
has effect: The subject drug produces the specific therapeutic or physiological effect described by the object entity.
has mechanism of action: The subject drug exerts its effect through the biological process or pathway described by the object entity.
has recommended dose duration: The subject drug requires the specified duration of regular dosing for its full therapeutic effect to be achieved.
is not: The subject drug does not belong to or possess the characteristic described by the object entity.
is not useful for: The subject drug is not effective in treating or managing the condition or type of pain described by the object entity.
normalizes: The subject entity regulates or brings back to normal the process or function described by the object entity.
results in: The subject drug leads to the physiological or therapeutic outcome described by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to manage or alleviate the medical condition described by the object entity.
